decisions.executionNote: Approach the near side of the straightedge symmetrically, keeping the initial arm configuration while checking gripper geometry.
Use very small increments to leave the initial singular configuration without a joint jump.
Gradually pitch both grippers toward the tabletop and approach the two ends of the straightedge.
Continue gradual downward pitching and bring each arm inward within its own workspace, above opposite portions of the straightedge.
Close the empty grippers and orient their tips downward for a two-point, table-level push on the straightedge rather than lifting any blocks.
Compensate tip height while finishing the downward pitch; keep the closed tips near the straightedge's near face, not beneath the cubes.
Advance both downward-pointing tips equally to contact the near edge of the straightedge and begin a level forward push.
The tips appear above the straightedge and the left end has shifted laterally. Reposition both contacts inward and lower behind the bar before pushing.
Withdraw behind the slightly skewed straightedge and clear its top. Re-establish contacts away from the ends before a coordinated forward-only push.
Clear the straightedge vertically and release any incidental contact before moving farther behind it; no cube is grasped.
Move well behind the straightedge with closed empty grippers before lowering; this avoids dragging its far face during repositioning.
Lower the closed tips behind the straightedge to the previously observed near-table contact height, without translating toward the blocks yet.
Advance the low closed tips from behind; the right contact should meet the skewed straightedge first and begin squaring it against the common push line.
Continue the symmetric, constant-height forward approach and inspect whether the straightedge rotates into two-point contact.
The straightedge is visibly rotating toward horizontal under the right contact. Continue equal forward motion to seat it against both tips.
The straightedge is now horizontal against both tips. Push it forward evenly toward the three cubes, maintaining the same table-level height.
The cubes are seating against the straightedge. Make a short, slow finishing push to square all three without lifting.
Withdraw straight backward from the near face, leaving the straightedge and seated cubes on the table; inspect the row before resetting.
Clear the work area, reopen the empty grippers, and begin a configuration-continuous return toward the initial poses.
All three cubes now appear seated in a straight parallel row. Continue resetting both arms through their own workspaces without disturbing the row.
Continue the smooth retreat toward the starting arm positions while restoring the original wrist orientation.
Reduce the final position and orientation offsets with smaller increments as both arms approach their original configuration.
